headline: DENISON'S PHOENIX MINE 24% COMPLETE — $161M Spent in First Construction Quarter; Q3 Profit CAD $81.77M
snippet: Denison Mines (TSX: DML) reported Q3 2026 results on November 4, confirming Phoenix ISR uranium mine is 24% complete after its first full quarter of construction with C$161.1M spent to date — against a first-production target of H2 2028. The company swung to a C$81.77M net profit (partly from financing income) and reported a new Phoenix North exploration drill hole returning 0.39% eU3O8 over 4.7 metres, an early-stage discovery adjacent to the production zone.

headline: ENERGY FUELS EARNS ON URANIUM, LOSES ON PAPER — $29.2M Q3 Revenue Up 65%; Korean REE Plant Online, White Mesa Heavy REE Circuit Approved
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU) posted Q3 2026 revenue of $29.2M (+65% YoY) on 320,000 lb uranium sales at a $88.90/lb average realized price — a third consecutive quarter of rising prices and a third consecutive quarter of uranium segment profit. The $52.4M net loss was largely non-cash securities write-downs; operationally, the company completed its Australian Strategic Materials acquisition in August, putting the Korean rare earth metals and alloys plant (1,300 t/yr NdFeB capacity) into service and receiving board approval for commercial-scale heavy rare earth oxide circuits at White Mesa Mill, expected complete in early 2028.

headline: EVERGREEN GOLD HITS 16m AT 5.1g/t FROM 61m — ASX:AGC Hillston Structure First Assays With 12 More Holes Still Pending
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) released first assays from its Evergreen Prospect in New South Wales on November 5, with the standout hole returning 16 metres at 5.1 g/t gold from 61 metres within the Hillston Structure. Only nine of 21 planned drill holes have returned assays, leaving 12 more pending — the assay trend from early holes will determine whether this intercept is a cluster outlier or a consistent zone.

headline: KINROSS UP 6.8%, AGNICO UP 5% — TSX Gold Miners Join Global Rally as Dollar Collapses on Midterm Results
snippet: Shares of the major TSX-listed gold miners surged on November 4 as a weaker US dollar amplified gold's climb above $4,100, with Kinross Gold gaining 6.8%, Agnico Eagle up 5%, and Barrick Mining and Newmont each advancing more than 5% in early trading. The rally caps a sharp recovery from October's intraday low near $3,875 — the product of a consensus-busting pullback from gold's January 2026 record of $5,595 — suggesting markets are pricing in a continued dollar-to-gold tailwind through year-end.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH TRUCE EXPIRES IN 5 DAYS — Nov. 10 Deadline Could Restore Broad Export Controls; Dysprosium and Yttrium Licenses Stay Regardless
snippet: China's suspension of its expanded October 2025 rare earth export controls — covering six MOFCOM announcements and paused by Announcement No. 70 — expires on November 10, 2026, in five days. Beijing has signalled case-by-case flexibility rather than a blanket renewal, but analysts identify full reimposition as one of three live outcomes; regardless of the decision, the April 2025 licensing regime for dysprosium, terbium, yttrium and three other heavy rare earths remains in force, maintaining a floor under supply constraints even if the broader suspension is extended.

headline: MP MATERIALS DOWN 53% FROM 52-WEEK HIGH — Goldman Cuts to $57, Morgan Stanley to $66 as Q3 2026 Earnings Land
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) fell 11.9% in October 2026 and enters Q3 earnings day trading roughly 53% below its 52-week high, with Goldman Sachs slashing its price target to $57 (from $65) and Morgan Stanley to $66 (from $73) during the month. Analysts expect revenue near $117M for Q3 — a year-over-year surge driven by NdPr sales growth after the company halted all Chinese concentrate sales in July 2025 — but the market is waiting on guidance language about critical minerals policy under the new Democratic majority before deciding whether to re-rate the stock.

headline: FORTUNA CONFIRMS GOLD IN SENEGAL — 1.9g/t Au Over 64m At Kabewest; $8M 51,000m Program Underway, Resource Estimate Due Q1 2027
snippet: Fortuna Mining (TSX: FVI) announced first drill results from the Kabewest prospect at its Bambadji Project in Senegal on November 2, with the lead intercept returning 1.9 g/t Au over an estimated 64 metres true width from 19 metres — confirming the structurally controlled gold mineralisation that surface work suggested. The initial 45-hole, 10,524-metre program is now complete, six rigs have been redeployed to the Wari and Latifa prospects, and an initial inferred resource estimate is targeted for Q1 2027 within an $8 million, 51,000-metre multi-prospect campaign.

headline: FALCON METALS GROWS OLSEN WELL GOLD ZONE 240m — ASX:FAL Second Hole Returns 16m @ 2.2g/t, Extending Discovery Footprint
snippet: Falcon Metals (ASX: FAL) released second-hole results from its Olsen Well gold discovery on November 2, with hole OWRC0007 returning 16 metres at 2.2 g/t gold from 8 metres depth, located approximately 240 metres from the original discovery hole. The result extends the known mineralised footprint at a prospect that is still at an early drill stage, consistent with an open, laterally continuous gold zone.

headline: CATALYST ONE PICKS UP BC RARE EARTH PROPERTY — $870K Deal Adds TSXV Junior to Growing British Columbia REE Land Rush
snippet: Catalyst One (TSXV: CTXCF) agreed to acquire a 100% interest in a rare earth exploration property in British Columbia from Lireca Resources for $870,000 in cash and shares plus a 3% net smelter return royalty, subject to TSXV acceptance. The deal adds Catalyst One to a growing list of junior companies staking positions in BC's rare earth corridor as the November 10 Chinese export control deadline approaches and the case for domestic North American REE supply strengthens.

headline: CHINA DEMANDS COPPER SUPPLY GUARANTEES AS ANGLO-TECK MERGER WAITS — SAMR Negotiating Remedies; March 2027 Close Target Holds
snippet: China's State Administration for Market Regulation remains the only regulator yet to approve the Anglo American–Teck Resources merger, with Beijing demanding steady copper concentrate supply commitments from Anglo American as a condition of clearance — a behavioural remedy pushed by Chinese smelters rather than an asset sale. Anglo American confirmed in an October 20 regulatory filing it still expects to close the deal by March 2027; CEO Stuart Chambers called the merger and an adjacent nickel asset sale 'test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities,' framing the negotiations as precedent-setting for future resource-sector M&A.
